parts.problem_md:
A teacher in the school has created a spreadsheet to display whether a student has good timekeeping when arriving at lessons. He has produced a formula but thinks it could be improved. The formula is:

=IF(B4>=A\$18,B\$18,IF(B4>=A\$17,B\$17,IF(B4>=A\$16,B\$16,IF(B4>=A\$15,B\$15,IF(B4>=A\$14,B\$14,"")))))

![Spreadsheet showing student lateness data per half term and a formula for assessing lateness rating with a legend for ratings from "Excellent" to "Very Poor".](assets/001-spreadsheet-showing-student-lateness-data-per-ha.png)

The teacher has improved the formula and has typed in =VLOOKUP(B4,A\$14:B\$18,2)

**Explain **the advantages of using this formula compared to the original one.
parts.solution_md:
Advantages of using this formula compared to the original one include:

Any **four **of the following:

- Quicker to type in the formula **[1 mark]**
- Fewer mistakes when typing in the formula **[1 mark]**
- Easier to spot mistakes **[1 mark]**
- Easier to expand the range **[1 mark]**
- Takes up less storage space **[1 mark]**
- Easier to remember when retyping **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A student is creating a spreadsheet of airports for a project.

![Spreadsheet with airport codes and names from various countries, including LHR for London Heathrow, MIL for Milan, and others from Italy, France, and Sweden.](assets/002-spreadsheet-with-airport-codes-and-names-from-va.png)

**Explain**, using examples, the differences between a function and a formula.
parts.solution_md:
The difference between a function and a formula are:

Max **two **of the following:

**Formula **

- A formula is a statement written by the user **[1 mark]**
- A formula is an equation **[1 mark]**
- A formula can contain values/references to cells/defined names **[1 mark]**
- A formula can contain functions **[1 mark]**

**One **mark for a valid example:

- =A1+B1, =SUM(A2:B2) **[1 mark]**

Max **two **of the following:

**Function **

- A function is a named piece of code designed to calculate specific values **[1 mark]**
- Functions are used inside formulas **[1 mark]**
- A function is a built in/predefined operation **[1 mark]**

**One** mark for a valid example

- =SUM/AVERAGE etc **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Tawara school has a shop that sells items needed by pupils in school. Part of a spreadsheet with details of the items is shown.

![Spreadsheet titled "Tawara School Shop" showing items, cost, selling price, profit, tax, amount sold, total profit per item, and total tax per item.](assets/003-spreadsheet-titled-tawara-school-shop-showing-it.png)

Tax is paid on certain items sold in the shop. The tax rate that has to be paid is 20% of the selling price. If tax is to be paid on an item, then ‘Y’ is placed underneath the Tax heading.

The formula in I4 is: IF(F4=''Y'',(\$I\$1*D4*G4),'''')

**Explain**, in detail, what the formula does.
parts.solution_md:
The formula is responsible for:

Any **five **of the following:

- If Tax is payable then//If F4 is equal to "Y" then **[1 mark]**
- If true the tax is paid **[1 mark]**
- Multiply the rate of tax/I1 … **[1 mark]**
- … by the selling price/D4 **[1 mark]**
- … by the amount sold/G4 **[1 mark]**
- If Tax is not payable//If F4 <>"Y"//Else//Otherwise … **[1 mark]**
- … then display a blank **[1 mark]**
- … the tax is not paid **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A doctor measures the blood pressure of some of his patients regularly. The patients take home a blood pressure machine and record their results on a spreadsheet which the doctor has created. Part of the spreadsheet is shown.

![Spreadsheet showing blood pressure readings from 10-16 Feb, with systolic, diastolic values, and warnings. Another section lists warning levels for reference.](assets/004-spreadsheet-showing-blood-pressure-readings-from.png)

When a reading produces a Severe or Low warning then the text automatically changes to a red font on a light red background.

**Explain **how the doctor could set up automatic colour change for these warnings on the spreadsheet.
parts.solution_md:
The doctor could set up automatic colour changes by:

Any **five **of the following:

- Highlight Column D **[1 mark]**
- Select Conditional Formatting **[1 mark]**
- Select Highlight Cell Rules **[1 mark]**
- Select Equal to Type in the Equal to box…**[1 mark]**
- Severe/Low Click on Format Select/Set the red font on light red background **[1 mark]**
- Repeat the process for Low/Severe **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
The doctor has set up a named range called Bloodpressure for the cells F3 to H7.

**Explain **why the doctor has used a named range.
parts.solution_md:
The doctor has used a named range due to:

Any **three **of the following:

- Removes the confusion over absolute and relative referencing **[1 mark]**
- Reduces the issues involved in changing the range **[1 mark]**
- Easier to understand the formula **[1 mark]**
- Easier to check for errors in the formula **[1 mark]**
- Easier to enter the formula **OR **Less errors in entering the formula **[1 mark]**
- Faster to write the name than to select the range **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
The formula =VLOOKUP(B3,Bloodpressure,3) has been entered into cell D3.

**Explain **what the formula does.
parts.solution_md:
The formula is responsible for:

Any **four **of the following:

- Looks up the value of B3 **[1 mark]**
- Looks in the named range Bloodpressure **[1 mark]**
- Returns the corresponding value... **[1 mark]**
- …from the 3rd column **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
You are creating a presentation on the World Games. You have created a spreadsheet showing the number of gold, silver and bronze medals awarded to different countries.

You are planning to create a graph in the presentation showing the country, the number of gold medals and the total number of medals.

![Table showing World Games Medals by country. Italy leads with 440 total medals, followed by the US with 382, Germany 386, and Russia 319.](assets/006-table-showing-world-games-medals-by-country-ital.png)

**Explain **how you would create a vertical bar chart, showing the name of the country, the number of gold medals and the total number of medals awarded to each country, on a new slide in the presentation.
parts.solution_md:
To create the bar chart you would need to:

Max **four **of the following:

- Open spreadsheet **[1 mark]**
- Load the file **[1 mark]**
- Select B3 to C13 **[1 mark]**
- Then hold CTRL and select F3 to F13 **[1 mark]**
- Click insert then click bar chart/graph **[1 mark]**
- Select the format/type of chart/graph **[1 mark]**
- Highlight the chart/graph **[1 mark]**
- Copy the bar chart/graph **[1 mark]**

**AND**

Max **four **of the following:

- Open the presentation software **[1 mark]**
- Add a new slide **[1 mark]**
- Click on new slide **[1 mark]**
- Paste the bar chart/graph **[1 mark]**
- Add titles/legend/axes labels **[1 mark]**
- Save the file **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Explain **how the data could be sorted by the total number of medals won by each country. The country with the largest number of medals should be at the top of the list.

parts.problem_md: **Explain** the differences between a VLOOKUP function and a LOOKUP function.
parts.solution_md:
Differences between a VLOOKUP function and a LOOKUP function include:

Any **three **of the following:

- LOOKUP allows for horizontal and vertical searching whereas VLOOKUP allows for vertical searching **[1 mark]**
- LOOKUP does not require an index value/only works on the second row/column whereas VLOOKUP requires an index value **[1 mark]**
- LOOKUP usually only works when the data is sorted VLOOKUP only returns data to the right of the searched column **[1 mark]**
- VLOOKUP user can select either an approximate or exact match to the lookup value **[1 mark]**
